evidence: outputs/agentic-workflow-benchmark/20260811T041553Z-evidence-v2/benchmark.json hashes all seven source evidence files and records Git, host, Python, and the aggregation command

The matched 660-frame robot comparison changes mean proxy score from 0.569684 to 0.864004, object lock from 0.028233 to 1.0, motion preservation from 0.035074 to 0.587255, and EPL minimum from 0.023541 to 0.545491
The AC-WM human-gated acceptance inventory is MiniMax-H3 0/3, posthoc single-pass OSCAR 1/3, and agentic selected-action OSCAR 2/3
docs/AGENTIC_WORKFLOW_BENCHMARKS.md records the complete matched tables, failed gates, sample counts, and scope boundaries
README.md exposes only the evidence-backed headline gains and preserves PARTIAL labels
lessons: Same-evaluator absolute deltas and authoritative human-gated yield are more defensible than averaging unrelated proxy scores.
Large aggregate gains can coexist with failed motion, EPL, topology, or human-review gates, so every headline must retain its acceptance status.
Agentic routing can improve both outcome yield and evaluation efficiency without proving cross-scene or physical generalization.
limitations: The main robot replacement comparison contains one retained real video, and AC-WM contains three selected action types in one real scene.
The evolved rightward AC-WM case is lift-then-carry-right rather than the rejected tabletop slide-right, so the 2/3 portfolio yield is not a same-action causal estimate.
The evidence is image-space, proxy, and deterministic 2-D fallback evidence; it does not establish robot-base control, physics, generalization, or real-robot execution.
next_actions: Repeat the frozen protocols on multiple held-out scenes, robot identities, and action types with confidence intervals.
Add calibrated robot-base trajectories and physical execution gates before claiming embodiment-independent control.
Keep human topology/contact review authoritative until a validated semantic evaluator covers the observed failure modes.
scope: retrospective quantitative benchmark of robot embodiment replacement and AC-WM agentic workflow evolution
summary: Matched evidence shows large proxy gains for robot embodiment replacement and raises AC-WM human-gated selected-action yield from 0/3 for the retained H3 baseline and 1/3 for posthoc single-pass OSCAR to 2/3, while failed gates and one-scene scope prevent an end-to-end success claim.
